samples.summary: New envelope-forwarding helper is not applied to the many other command sites, which still discard a real backend envelope (e.g. SESSION_EXPIRED) as `{code:"ERROR"}`
samples.evidence: `forwardUpstreamError`/`upstreamErrorJson` are wired into only 6 command sites (docs/notes/slides content+export) and the import/upload/download orchestrators. Every other site still does `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)` — docs.ts:80,107,121,139,157; notes.ts:40,67,81,99,117; slides.ts:45,72,86,104,122; cells.ts:25,65,91,143; tabs.ts:16,49,75; files.ts:86,106,124,142; api-keys.ts:18,32,46. That path throws away the response body entirely, including bodies that *are* the documented envelope: `HttpClient.sessionExpiredBody()` (http-client.ts:157) returns `{error:{code:'SESSION_EXPIRED',message:'Session expired. Run `wafflebase login`.'}}` with `ok:false, status:401` (http-client.ts:181), so `wafflebase docs get <id>` on an expired JWT session emits `{error:{code:"ERROR",message:"HTTP 401"}}` and the actionable `code` an agent is supposed to branch on is lost. Same for any backend envelope on those endpoints. The change makes the CLI's error contract depend on which subcommand was run, which is exactly what the new helper's doc comment says must not happen.

samples.summary: `waitForLoadState("networkidle")` inside waitForFontsReady is not best-effort, so an unreachable fonts host still hard-fails the capture despite the comment claiming otherwise
samples.evidence: The header comment (lines 340-342, 388-394) states the harness "never hard-depends on fonts.googleapis.com being reachable" and that only steps 3/4 are wrapped in `settle`. But line 386 `await page.waitForLoadState("networkidle")` is unwrapped and now runs *after* section mount (i.e. after the mount-triggered Google Fonts requests are in flight). If those requests hang rather than fail fast, `waitForLoadState` rejects on its 30s default timeout and the exception propagates out of `capturePass`, aborting the whole run — the exact failure mode the comment promises is avoided.

samples.summary: Catch-all font poll `status !== "loading"` is satisfied trivially by faces that have not started loading
samples.evidence: `[...document.fonts].every((face) => face.status !== "loading")` passes immediately for faces in `status: "unloaded"` — i.e. any registered face whose fetch has not begun yet (a late-injected @font-face link, or a face Chromium has not requested because no laid-out text needs it yet). The poll's first tick can therefore succeed while the very fetches it is meant to await are still pending, so the advertised guarantee ("covers families nobody thought to list here") does not hold.

samples.summary: `settle`'s timeout detection swallows any error whose message merely contains the substring "timeout"
samples.evidence: `if (!/Timeout .* exceeded|timeout/i.test(message)) throw error;` — the second alternative is a bare case-insensitive `timeout` substring test, so genuine harness bugs whose messages happen to mention a timeout (navigation/protocol errors, a page error string, `Target closed ... timeout`) are downgraded to a warning and the capture proceeds with an unknown page state, contradicting the doc comment two lines above ("Anything that is not a timeout still throws").

samples.summary: On the `ok && !bytes` branch, `upstreamErrorJson` now reports a success status as the error message (`HTTP 200`)
samples.evidence: `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes) io.stderr(upstreamErrorJson(res));` — when the response succeeded but carried no bytes, `upstreamErrorJson` formats `HTTP ${res.status}` from the *success* status, producing `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP 200'}}`, which reads as if the server returned 200 as a failure. The previous code emitted a bare `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}` here. A distinct code/message (e.g. EMPTY_RESPONSE) is needed for that branch.

samples.summary: `isErrorEnvelope` accepts an empty-string `code`, forwarding an envelope that `outputError` would itself reject as unusable
samples.evidence: `typeof (err as {code?: unknown}).code === 'string'` admits `code: ''`, so `{error:{code:''}}` is forwarded verbatim with exit 1. `errorCode` in the same file (line 44) deliberately requires `code.length > 0` before trusting a code, so the two acceptance rules in one module disagree and an agent branching on `error.code` gets an empty string with no `HTTP_ERROR` fallback.

samples.summary: Documented error-code contract now contradicts the code: README says non-typed failures report "ERROR", but content/export paths emit HTTP_ERROR
samples.evidence: README's Output Conventions state typed codes are `INVALID_DOCX`, `TYPE_MISMATCH`, `CONFIRMATION_REQ` and "everything else reports \"ERROR\"". After this change `docs|notes|slides content/export` emit `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR', ...}}` for every non-envelope upstream failure (formatter.ts:138), while sibling commands like `docs get` still emit `ERROR` for the same condition. The doc comment on `upstreamErrorJson` cites only `skills/docs-import-docx.md` (import paths) as the promise for HTTP_ERROR; nothing documents it for the content/export paths.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. `forwardUpstreamError`/`upstreamErrorJson` exist (formatter.ts:162,186) and are wired only into docs.ts:197,249, notes.ts:148,195, slides.ts:154,197 and the import/upload/download orchestrators. A repo-wide grep confirms all other cited sites still do `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)` (docs.ts:80,107,121,139,157; notes.ts:40,67,81,99,117; slides.ts:45,72,86,104,122; cells.ts:25,65,91,143; tabs.ts:16,49,75; files.ts:86,106,124,142; api-keys.ts:18,32,46), discarding res.data; the surrounding catch routes to outputError, whose errorCode() (formatter.ts:41-47) yields 'ERROR'. The loss is reachable on a real path: HttpClient.sessionExpiredBody() (http-client.ts:157-164) returns the {code:'SESSION_EXPIRED'} envelope and request() returns it as {ok:false,status:401,data:envelope} (http-client.ts:180-182) whenever a JWT refresh fails (send(), lines 133-154), so `docs get` prints {"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 401"}}. No guard elsewhere converts it — 'SESSION_EXPIRED' occurs nowhere else in CLI source. Swallowing/mis-handling an upstream failure code is squarely in the Correctness lane, and the helper's own doc comment (formatter.ts:129-136) states the code must not depend on which command was run. The task file's Non-goals narrow the task, not this lens's rubric, and I may not refute merely because the change did not touch those lines.

finding.summary: Non-envelope backend error bodies now lose their `message` entirely — Nest's detailed 400/403/404 messages are replaced by a bare `HTTP <status>`
finding.evidence: `isErrorEnvelope` only accepts `{error:{code:string}}`. The backend produces that shape for exactly one case (`TYPE_MISMATCH_BODY`, packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:42). Every other failure is a stock Nest exception — e.g. `throw new BadRequestException("Invalid block at ${path}: 'id' must be a non-empty string")` (docs-content.controller.ts:260), `NotFoundException('Document has no file')` (files.controller.ts:141), `ForbiddenException('This API key does not have write access')` (files.controller.ts:81) — which serialize to `{message, error:'Bad Request', statusCode}`. Before this change those bodies were printed verbatim, so the operator saw *which* block was invalid or *why* access was denied. Now `upstreamErrorJson` returns `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP 400'}}` and `forwardUpstreamError` throws `HTTP 400` into `outputError`, discarding the only diagnostic the server sent. Rejecting the mis-shaped envelope is right; dropping the `message` string with it is a real regression in error reporting on the most common failure paths (validation, auth, not-found) across docs/notes/slides import, files upload/download and all six content/export commands. Folding a string `body.message` (or `body.error` when it is a string) into the synthesized envelope's `message` would preserve it.

verdict.reason: The claimed regression is not present. formatter.ts already extracts and preserves the non-envelope body's `message`: `upstreamDetail` (formatter.ts:104-121) reads a string `body.message`, joins a class-validator string array with '; ', accepts a bare string body, trims, skips HTML documents, and truncates at 500 chars; `upstreamMessage` (formatter.ts:124-127) returns `HTTP <status>: <detail>` whenever a detail exists. `forwardUpstreamError` throws `UpstreamHttpError(upstreamMessage(res), status)` (formatter.ts:171) and `upstreamErrorJson` synthesizes `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR', message: upstreamMessage(res)}}` (formatter.ts:191-195). So Nest bodies like `NotFoundException('Document has no file')` or `ForbiddenException('This API key does not have write access')` surface as `HTTP 404: Document has no file` / `HTTP 403: ...`, not a bare `HTTP <status>`. Tests assert exactly this (upstream-error.test.ts:80-96, 241-245, 247-255). The bare `HTTP <status>` form only occurs for null/undefined/HTML bodies, where there is no diagnostic text to keep. The remedy the finding proposes ("folding a string body.message into the synthesized envelope's message") is already the implemented behavior; the only unfolded field is the generic string label `body.error` ('Bad Request'), which duplicates the status code and carries no diagnostic content.
